entries.clue: Finally enjoy prize after good turn (6)

indicatorNotes.Finally: takes only the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: to prize something is to rate it highly

annotation.surface: Someone does a good turn and finally gets to enjoy a prize for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good turn' reads as a kind deed, but good is only G and turn is the definition. 'After' puts G first, so the order is G, then Y, then RATE.
annotation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to turn or spin round and round.

entries.clue: Leave a fitness class, finding yourself off the deep end (5,3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Going ape' is a verb phrase; 'finding yourself off the deep end' is the sense it replaces.

blocks.note: a going is a leaving, a departure
PE = physical education, the school gym lesson

annotation.surface: Someone walks out of a gym class, feeling out of their depth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off the deep end' sounds like a swimming lesson, which suits the fitness class, but here it means losing your temper or going mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Going ape and going off the deep end both mean losing control in anger or excitement.

entries.clue: One with a compass – point’s lost by him? (7)

blocks.note: a hiker navigating the countryside by compass
not a compass point but the point of a story, which a long-winded talker loses

annotation.surface: A hiker with a compass somehow still loses his way to the next point.
annotation.walkthrough: The compass makes 'point' look like a compass point; a RAMBLER is both a country walker and someone who talks on without getting to the point.
annotation.definitionFit: The word covers two people at once: the hiker with a map and compass, and the digressive talker.

entries.clue: Drink the writer raised, it honours a family (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting a word upward writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
the writer = ME, the setter talking about himself; turned upward it is EM

annotation.surface: A writer raises a glass in a toast to honour a family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a glass raised in a toast, but it turns ME round. A totem stands for a clan or family group.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem venerated by a family or clan as its symbol.

entries.clue: Perhaps clubs holding all that remains: hands seen at ends of these? (8)

annotation.definition: hands seen at ends of these?

indicatorNotes.holding: the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: clubs are an example of arms, weapons; 'perhaps' flags the example

annotation.surface: A card player asks whether all that is left in the hand is clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: Clubs, hands and remains all point to a card game; clubs are in fact weapons. Your hands rest at the ends of a chair's armrests.
annotation.definitionFit: Armrests are the arms of a chair, where your hands lie at the far end.

entries.clue: Looked back on scripture lessons: cool! (11)

blocks.note: RE = religious education, the school subject

annotation.surface: Someone thinks back fondly on their old scripture classes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool!' reads as a schoolchild's exclamation, but it is an adjective meaning calm. RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
annotation.definitionFit: To recollect something is to remember it, to look back on it.

entries.clue: Copy badly executed procedure (9)

indicatorNotes.badly executed: something carried out badly comes out jumbled

annotation.surface: A botched procedure produced a poor copy.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator sits between definition and fodder and reads naturally as describing the procedure.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to make a duplicate of a picture or document.

entries.clue: Part of Croatian city on high (5,2)

blocks.note: Split is a port on the Croatian coast

annotation.surface: A travel note about a hilltop quarter of a Croatian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a noun, a district of the city, but it is the verb: to part is to separate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to separate, as a couple ending a relationship does.

entries.clue: Hunts, in scrubs (6)

blocks.note: to scour an area is to search it thoroughly
to scour a pan is to scrub it

annotation.surface: Someone searches, dressed in hospital scrubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrubs' reads as the clothes surgeons wear; here it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Scour means both to search hard and to scrub clean.

entries.clue: Section of certain material one may wish to escape (6)

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

annotation.surface: Some cloth or text you would rather get away from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One may wish to escape' reads as describing the material; it is a person who wants to break out.
annotation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone who may wish to escape.

entries.clue: Somewhere in Mexico, a Catholic by cupola, trembling (8)

indicatorNotes.trembling: letters that tremble are shaken into a new order

annotation.surface: A Catholic stands shaking beside a church dome somewhere in Mexico.
annotation.walkthrough: The domes and Catholics fit Mexico perfectly, which hides that cupola's letters are simply being shaken up.
annotation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast.

entries.clue: Good old crossword setter: lad’s flipping getting top award (4,5)

indicatorNotes.flipping: a word flipped over reads backwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as ME

annotation.surface: A veteran crossword setter's son is thrilled at winning first prize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a British mild oath, as in 'flipping heck', but it turns LAD round.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: in the Olympics and elsewhere, first place wins this over silver and bronze.

entries.clue: Casting out money and Red Book (11)

indicatorNotes.Casting: casting metal reshapes it, so the letters are remoulded

annotation.surface: Someone throws out cash along with a little red book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Casting out' looks like a phrase meaning throwing away; only 'Casting' is the indicator and 'out' is fodder. Red Book is a decoy for Mao's Little Red Book.
annotation.definitionFit: Deuteronomy is the fifth book of the Old Testament.

entries.clue: River creature getting closer in Cockney’s game (5)

indicatorNotes.Cockney’s: Cockneys drop their H's, so the H goes

blocks.note: in the children's hiding game, a seeker getting closer is told 'getting hotter'
a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the initial H
names the hiding game where the seeker hears this; contributes no letters

annotation.surface: A river animal edging nearer during a Londoner's game.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'game' is hunt-the-thimble, where 'warmer' and 'hotter' tell the seeker they are closing in; the Cockney accent then knocks off the H.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by habitat: a web-footed fish-eating mammal that lives along riverbanks.

entries.clue: Leisure activity from which you may hope to be dropped? (9,4)

annotation.definition: Leisure activity from which you may hope to be dropped?

blocks.note: a hobby or pastime, taken at face value

blocks.clueFragment: from which you may hope to be dropped?
blocks.note: surface: a hobby so dull you want to be thrown out of it; setter: something you are literally dropped from, an aircraft

annotation.surface: A hobby so dull you would rather be kicked out of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' suggests being thrown out of a group or team; skydivers are dropped from the plane, and they very much hope to be.
annotation.definitionFit: The sport is a leisure pursuit whose whole point is being dropped from a height.

entries.clue: Punch a tenor, getting personal in area with many restaurants (9)

blocks.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
T = tenor, as in SATB choir parts
your own = personal to you; 'getting' just adds it on

annotation.surface: A brawl breaks out when someone punches a tenor in a restaurant district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting personal' reads as a fight turning nasty, but it just adds OWN. Chin as a verb, to hit on the chin, is informal British.
annotation.definitionFit: A Chinatown is a city's Chinese quarter, known for its many restaurants.

entries.clue: Those intoning M-A-G-I-C? (8)

blocks.note: people chanting, as a wizard chants an incantation
the hyphens show the word said letter by letter; 'magic' tempts you towards casting spells

annotation.surface: Wizards chanting magic words.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intoning magic' suggests wizards chanting spells; the hyphens show someone simply spelling out a word letter by letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Spellers are people who spell out words, letter by letter.

entries.clue: Esther shortly dons formal footwear, makes timely investment (6,3,4)

indicatorNotes.shortly: cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.dons: the footwear puts on Esther like clothing, around her

blocks.note: a pump is a light shoe

annotation.surface: Esther puts on smart shoes before making a well-timed investment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Formal footwear' looks like one phrase for smart shoes, but it is two pieces, and Esther sits between them. Priming the pump means spending now to get something going.
annotation.definitionFit: To prime the pump is to invest money at the right moment to stimulate growth.

entries.clue: Grandeur that is retrograde, Everyman’s a tragic relic of former times (7)

annotation.definition: a tragic relic of former times

indicatorNotes.retrograde: going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: that is = IE (id est), written backwards
the setter, Everyman, speaking of himself is I

annotation.surface: A pompous setter describes himself as a sad old relic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Everyman's a tragic relic' reads as the setter's self-mockery; the 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pompeii is the Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, a tragic relic of the ancient world.

entries.clue: Perfect, working out pain (7)

indicatorNotes.working: letters put to work are moved into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Exercising away your pain is perfect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working out' reads as exercise, but only 'working' is the indicator and 'out' is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopian describes an ideal, perfect state.

entries.clue: Ancient Greece’s artisanal trinkets’ expensive stones, primarily? (6)

annotation.definition: Ancient Greece’s artisanal trinkets’ expensive stones, primarily?

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the primary, first, letter of each word

annotation.surface: A museum label on the precious stones in ancient Greek craftwork.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: its initials spell the answer, and agates were indeed used in ancient Greek jewellery.
annotation.definitionFit: Agates are semi-precious banded stones used in ancient jewellery and carvings.

entries.clue: After a month, publication rejected letter from Athens (5)

indicatorNotes.After: the publication is written after the month
indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the whole thing reads backwards

annotation.surface: A month on, a magazine turns down a letter from Greece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' sits beside 'publication' as if something sent to the editor, but it is an alphabet letter. A, M and MAG give AMMAG, which reversed is GAMMA.
annotation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Traditionalists hold out with loco beliefs in the end (3,6)

indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are out of order
indicatorNotes.in the end: takes only the end letter of beliefs

annotation.surface: Conservatives stubbornly cling to their crazy beliefs until the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold out' reads as a phrase for resisting, but 'out' is the anagram indicator acting on HOLD, LOCO and the S.
annotation.definitionFit: The old school are those who keep to traditional ways.

entries.clue: Bird that’s seen on building site (5)

annotation.surface: A bird spotted on a construction site.
annotation.walkthrough: It reads as one bird in one place; it is two different cranes.
annotation.definitionFit: A crane is both a wading bird and a tall lifting machine on building sites.

entries.clue: English books thrice rejected, embroiling English again in confrontation (3-2-3)

indicatorNotes.embroiling: drawing E into the middle of it

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament books, three times

annotation.surface: An English literature row over three rejected books turns into a face-off.
annotation.walkthrough: E plus OT three times, reversed, makes TOTOTOE; the second E goes in after the first TO.
annotation.definitionFit: Toe-to-toe means standing face to face in direct confrontation.

entries.clue: Dog tooth (6)

blocks.note: the adjective for dogs, also used as a noun for one

annotation.walkthrough: 'Dog tooth' reads as one thing, even a fabric pattern, but it is two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: A canine is a dog, and also the pointed tooth beside the incisors.

entries.clue: Secret agent’s drinking in pub by Earl’s woodland (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The answer is plural; 'woodland' is a mass noun covering several spinneys.

indicatorNotes.drinking: the agent takes the pub and earl inside, as if swallowing them

blocks.note: SPY plus the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: A spy drinks in the pub next to an aristocrat's woods.
annotation.walkthrough: The spy really is drinking in a pub on the surface; in the wordplay SPYS drinks INN and E. A spinney is a small wood, a British word.
annotation.definitionFit: Spinneys are small woods or copses, so together they make woodland.

entries.clue: Plays safe in t-shirts, to some extent (6)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: Someone takes no risks by staying in t-shirts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plays safe' reads as one phrase, but 'Plays' alone is the definition, in the sense of a feint or dummy move in sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Feints are deceptive moves or plays in fencing, boxing or football.
